grades.quote: Section 3.5.2 explains decay usage scheduling, a dynamic adjustment policy commonly used in general-purpose computing environments.
grades.reason: It only introduces decay usage scheduling as a dynamic priority adjustment policy for general-purpose systems. It does not explain why a thread that wakes after waiting is favored over one that recently used the CPU.

It covers fair-share and proportional-share scheduling. It never mentions decay-usage scheduling or how recent CPU usage changes priority. It also says a thread that waited gets no catch-up block, which is a different mechanism.
